correctness.rationale: The original system differentiates exactly to \(\ddot v+\beta\dot v=\alpha v^p\), and the monotone phase parameter obeys \(\frac{d}{dv}Y^2=2\alpha v^p-2\beta Y\). Positive solutions eventually have increasing memory coordinates and reach infinite amplitude in finite time. Iterating the integrated energy equation produces \(Y=cv^q+dv+ev^{2-q}+R\), with a provably integrable remainder \(R\) for all \(q>2\). The counterterm-renormalized energy has exactly the derivative \(\mathcal K_q'= -2\beta R\) and hence converges, with the claimed three error exponents. At \(q=3\), exact algebra yields the logarithmic energy coefficient \(-3\beta^3/(16c)\) and phase-velocity coefficient \(-9\beta^3/(32\alpha)\). The packaged symbolic checker confirms only these coefficient identities; analytic inequalities establish the infinite limit. The estimates concern each fixed positive orbit, not a uniform-in-initial-data bound. Comparing two positive phase velocities at one fixed memory coordinate gives an exact linear equation for their positive squared difference and its strictly positive limit, proving the finite part is strictly ordered by initial phase velocity.

value.rationale: When damping vanishes the second-order phase equation has conserved mechanical energy. Under positive damping the same quantity diverges. The finding identifies the universal polynomial terms and the last necessary counterterm that extract a finite energy-like orbit invariant for all powers \(p>3\). Its sharp exponent threshold \(p=5\) separates a divergent fractional-power drift, a nonzero logarithmic drift, and uncorrected convergence. This is a structural singularity classification with a controlled integrable remainder, rather than a renaming or merely a leading blow-up-rate estimate. The finite part distinguishes trajectories and supports asymptotic matching; no claims are made about arbitrary delay kernels. The finite-part constant is not merely existential: a positive integral formula proves strict ordering of all trajectories sharing a fixed starting memory coordinate and increasing phase velocity, giving it concrete discriminative significance.
